subject: Clarify prefix caching charges and proposed volume discount
messages:
From: Samira Patel <s.patel@acme.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Understanding how prefix caching affects billing for Acme pilot

Hi Diego / Camila,

Quick one while we finalise the SOW: our engineering team is planning to use prefix (prompt) caching heavily for a common onboarding flow that contains a ~700-token system prompt + a 40-token user instruction. Typical requests are a short 50–120 token completion.

Before we sign up for the pilot, can you confirm how Redwood bills for requests when a prefix/prompt cache hit occurs? Specific asks:
- If a response is served entirely from the cache (identical prefix + inputs), do we get charged for the prompt tokens, completion tokens, or both?
- If the cache serves part of the response (e.g., KV cache that avoids regen for the first N tokens), how is billing split?
- Any differences between hosted API baseline pricing vs. enterprise committed plans?

Also, we need a simple worked example we can share with procurement showing the bills for a 100k requests/day scenario with 70% cache-hit rate. Are there published examples or a template you can share?

We have the SOW draft but procurement asked for explicit per-token math so they can compare to other vendors.

Thanks — can we sync tomorrow for 30 minutes?

Samira
Procurement, Acme Corp
procure@acme-acme.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Understanding how prefix caching affects billing for Acme pilot

Samira — thanks for the clear scenario. Short answers up front, then a worked example and next steps below. I attached our pricing_model_v3.xlsx with an example tab for prefix-heavy workloads.

High level billing rules (hosted API baseline):
- If a response is served entirely from the cache (a full cache hit), we charge a small lookup/unit fee rather than full prompt tokens. That lookup fee compensates for metadata/serving costs but is materially lower (order-of-magnitude) than generating the response.
- If the request triggers any model generation (even for a few tokens) we bill for the prompt tokens consumed plus the generation (completion) tokens as normal. Partial cache usages that avoid some generation are billed proportional to the tokens actually generated.
- For enterprise/committed plans we can convert those lookup fees into effective per-request credits and offer explicit tiered discounts against both generation and prompt charges.

Worked example (summary) — full math is in the attached spreadsheet:
- Assumptions: 100k requests/day, average prompt length 740 tokens (system + user), average completion 80 tokens, cache-hit rate 70% (full hits), remaining 30% are cold and require full generation.
- Baseline hosted list prices (example): prompt $0.000060/token, completion $0.000120/token, cache-lookup $0.0005/request (when full hit).
- Daily cost:
  * Cache-hit portion (70k reqs): 70k * $0.0005 = $35/day (lookup fees only)
  * Cold portion (30k reqs): 30k * ((740 * $0.000060) + (80 * $0.000120)) = 30k * ($0.0444 + $0.0096) = 30k * $0.054 = $1,620/day
  * Total ~ $1,655/day => ~$49,650/month

Key takeaways: significant cache hit rates materially reduce cost because repeated prompt tokens (740 tokens) are not billed when served from cache — you only pay the lightweight lookup. If you want guaranteed thresholds for budgeting we can map the lookup fee to an effective per-token equivalent for comparison.

Commercial options / discounts:
- Pilot: we can grant $10k in platform credits for the initial 30-day pilot (applies to lookups + generation).
- Committed volume tiers: 10% discount at $25k/month committed, 15% at $50k/month, 22% at $100k/month. We can also convert lookup fees into committed-request buckets (e.g., 1M cached lookups/mo).

Next steps:
1) If you can confirm expected daily request volume profile (percent full hits vs partial), I’ll populate the spreadsheet with exact math for procurement.
2) I’ll loop in Finance to draft a term sheet showing the discount for ACME-2026-0812.
3) Proposed time: 2026-04-19 10:00 PT for a 30-min sync — does that work?

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Understanding how prefix caching affects billing for Acme pilot

Diego — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of clarifying points so we can get procurement comfortable: 
1) For partial cache avoids (your ‘partial’ case), is the billing granularity per-token (i.e., we are billed exactly for the tokens generated) or is there a minimum charged quantum once any generation happens?
2) Does the cache-lookup fee count against rate limits or concurrency quotas in any way? Our infra team is concerned cached responses should not consume the same concurrent GPU capacity as fresh generations.

Quick numbers from our side to populate your spreadsheet:
- 100k req/day (peak 150k/day)
- Estimated full-hit 70%, partial-hit 10% (some prefix matched but requires additional regen), cold 20%
- Average completion when generated: 60 tokens

If you can drop these into the exact math and call out the monthly invoice delta (hosted list vs 15% committed at $50k), that’ll make procurement happier. We can do the 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. 

Also please include an itemised line we can show to our legal/procure team that explains what we’re billed for when we use KV/prefix caches (simple one-liner they can put into the SOW).

Thanks — Samira
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@acme.com>, procure@acme-acme.com
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Understanding how prefix caching affects billing for Acme pilot

Samira — great questions. I updated the attached pricing_model_v3.xlsx (tab: ACME_workup) with your profile (100k/day, 70/10/20 split) and produced two columns (hosted list vs committed 15% @ $50k). Full working is in the sheet but summary below.

Billing granularity:
- We bill per token generated for any generation that occurs. There is no hidden minimum once generation starts — if 2 tokens are generated we bill for those 2 tokens. Partial savings scale linearly with generated token count.
- Cache-lookup fees do not consume GPU generation capacity. They are served from the cache tier and are accounted separately from model concurrency/slot limits. You will not see cached responses occupying inference GPUs; they have separate throughput accounting.

Updated numbers (monthly):
- Hosted list: ~$48,800/month (your split and averages applied)
- Committed $50k/month with 15% discount: net ~$42,500/month (includes conversion of 1M cached lookups/mo into committed credits)

SOW wording (one-liner for procurement/legal):
"When a request is fully served from prefix/KV cache, the customer is billed a cache-lookup service fee; when model generation occurs, billing is charged per actual prompt and completion tokens generated. Partial cache usage is billed pro-rated to the number of tokens generated."

Commercially, we recommend a $50k/month committed plan for Acme for predictable unit economics and included committed cached-lookup credits. For the pilot we’ll apply $10k credits and a 30-day evaluation. I’ve attached a redlineable SOW (acme_multipage_sow.pdf) and the updated pricing workbook.

Next: I’ll have our finance lead send a short term sheet (HS-12345678) and Camila will coordinate signature logistics. Talk tomorrow 10:00 PT — invite incoming.

Best,
